title: Tail Latency Sentencing and Capacity Escalation Procedure
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview:

This document defines a deterministic operational process for handling persistent tail-latency regressions that threaten SLOs and consumption of error budgets, plus the capacity-escalation steps to preserve SLOs while keeping customer impact minimal. It combines: SLO detection thresholds, automated tooling actions, human escalation steps, capacity provisioning templates, and incident-review evidence requirements.

Scope and applicability:
- Services: primarily applies to inference-api, embedding-service, and request-proxy.
- Workloads: real-time token generation (interactive), batch embeddings, and streaming outputs.
- Audience: SRE on-call, runtime engineers, capacity owners, product stewards.

Goals:
- Detect tail-latency regressions before an SLO breach and enact containment within 15 minutes.
- Provide clear capacity escalation steps to restore headroom within 60 minutes for hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Ensure incident reviews capture capacity decisions and cost trade-offs for continuous improvement.

Key definitions:
- Tail latency: p99 latency for generation requests measured at the API ingress.
- Error budget: configured per SLO window; burn rate is unitless ratio over 1 indicating accelerated consumption.
- Headroom: the margin (%) between current sustained load and provisioned throughput at the target SLO.

SLOs (example canonical service):
| service | metric | SLO target | evaluation window | alert threshold |
| inference-api | p99 latency (gen, 0–1024 tokens) | < 450 ms | 30d | p99 > 400 ms for 10m |
| inference-api | availability (5xx) | >= 99.9% | 30d | 5xx rate > 0.1% for 5m |
| embedding-service | 95th latency | < 200 ms | 30d | p95 > 180 ms for 15m |

Detection and pre-flight checks (automated):
1) Alert triggers:
   - Telemetry: alert when p99 exceeds "alert threshold" in SLO table AND burn_rate > 1.2 over a 10-minute window.
   - Synthetic canary fail: synthetic-canary-p99>threshold (see Synthetic testing below).
2) Automated triage run (scripted, < 3m):
   - Gather recent traces for affected request path: run `rbctl traces fetch --service=inference-api --since=15m --out=/tmp/traces.json`
   - Snapshot instance CPU/GPU utilization: `rbctl telemetry snapshot --service=inference-api --since=15m`
   - Check autoscaler status: `ri-autoscaler status --pool inference-gpu-pool`
   - If KV-cache hit rate < 80% and p99 elevated, tag impact as `cache-warm` in the incident ticket.

Containment and immediate mitigations (15 minute target):
- If p99 > 600 ms: automatically reduce concurrency on non-critical routes via traffic-shepherd: `trafficctl throttle --service=inference-api --routes='/batch,/async' --p=0.5` (engineers: this throttles to 50% of normal QPS).
- If 5xx spike accompanied: activate circuit-breaker policy for long-running requests: `rbctl policy apply --name=long-run-circuit`
- Evict or deprioritize low-priority tenants using tenant-priority tool: `tenantctl set-priority --tenants-file=low_priority_list.json --mode=soft-evict`

Capacity escalation (when automated mitigations insufficient; 60 minute target):
Trigger criteria (any one):
- Headroom < 15% sustained for 10m and burn_rate > 2.0
- Autoscaler capped at max_replicas and p99 remains above SLO target
- Repeated synthetic-canary failures after warm-up

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Notify on-call and capacity-owner Slack channel: `#sre-capacity-escalation` with brief: service, current p99, burn_rate, headroom, suspected cause.
2. Apply short-term capacity bump (hot-path):
   - Hosted: request immediate burst from cloud: runbook-runner `ri request-burst --pool inference-gpu-pool --gpus 2 --until=PT4H` (SRE has approval scope up to +4 GPUs per pool).
   - Dedicated: enable reserved hot-burst policy: `terraform apply -var='hot_burst=true' modules/dedicated/pool` (checkout branch `hot-burst-<incident-id>`).
   - Private: follow customer upgrade procedure (see `eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/customer-urgent-burst-sla`), notify customer success.
3. Adjust batching/quantization knobs for affected model routes (if safe):
   - Use `model-ops adjust --model=redwood/gpt-opt-1 --batch_size=64 --quant-profile=fast` for temporary throughput gains.
   - Document change in incident ticket; revert after stability confirmed.
4. Prep longer-term capacity expansion if headroom unlikely to return: open a capacity PR with metrics, requested commit, cost delta, and approval flow (see Capacity PR template below).

Capacity PR template (required when escalation changed long-term capacity):
| field | value |
| title | [INCIDENT-ID] Capacity commit request for inference-gpu-pool |
| requested increase | +X GPUs / +N slots (specify exact instance type) |
| anticipated SLO impact | p99 expected reduction from A -> B |
| cost delta | estimated $/month |
| rollback plan | steps and owner |

Operational tooling reference (commands and dashboards):
- Dashboards:
  - inference-api/p99-overview (primary)
  - capacity/orchestration-pool-health (shows pool headroom and warm pool counts)
- Alerts (Alertmanager names):
  - SRE:inference-api-p99-high (thresholds match SLO table)
  - SRE:inference-api-error-budget-burnrate-high
  - Ops:pool-autoscaler-saturation
- Useful CLI utilities:
  - rbctl (runtime bootstrap & traces) — `rbctl help`
  - trafficctl (throttles & routing) — `trafficctl list-policies`
  - tenantctl (tenant prioritization) — `tenantctl status`
  - ri (runbook integrator) — `ri run handoff --incident=INC-1234`
  - synthetic harness: `python tools/synthetic_load.py --service=inference-api --qps=50 --duration=300 --model=gpt-small`

Synthetic testing matrix (before/after capacity changes):
| scenario | qps | payload | acceptable p99 | notes |
| warm-cache steady | 50 | 512 tokens | < 450 ms | baseline expected |
| burst 5x | 250 | 256 tokens | < 550 ms | validates autoscaler response |
| cold-start mix | 30 | 1024 tokens | < 700 ms | measures KV-cache warm-up |

Incident review evidence checklist (required for postmortem):
- Timeline with minute-level events (alert fired, automation run, manual mitigations, capacity changes).
- Telemetry snapshots (traces, heatmaps, pool utilization) attached.
- List of runbook commands executed and who executed them (copy+paste command output where possible).
- Capacity PRs/approvals and cost delta calculations.
- Customer impact summary (top affected tenants, request types, estimated affected requests).
- Decision log: why did we change capacity vs. degrade traffic vs. change quantization?

Post-incident review rubric (how we grade actions):
1) Detection: Were alerts actionable and timely? (Score: 1–5)
2) Containment: Were mitigations applied within the 15m target? (Score: 1–5)
3) Stewardship: Were capacity requests scoped and cost-conscious? (Score: 1–5)
4) Documentation: Were decisions and artifacts preserved in the ticket? (Pass/Fail)
5) Root cause clarity: Do the owners agree on RCA and next steps? (Pass/Fail)

Runbook escalation matrix (who to call in order):
1. On-call SRE (primary pager) — execute steps up to automated mitigations.
2. Runtime engineer (model serving team) — adjust model ops knobs and validate quantization safety.
3. Capacity owner (gpu-fleet) — approve hot-burst and run terraform/ri steps.
4. Product steward — coordinate customer communication if dedicated/private tenants impacted.
5. Director of SRE — if cost delta or capacity PR exceeds 2x typical monthly commit.

Operational play notes and cautions:
- Avoid rolling quantization or model weight changes during peak traffic unless you have a canary path. Document and notify product + on-call.
- Hot-burst is a short stopgap. Always create a capacity PR for durable changes and include rollback windows.
- Prefer traffic-shaping and tenant-priority first for short incidents to avoid cost surprises.
- If automated mitigations are repeatedly used for weeks against the same pattern, schedule a reliability initiative and capacity experiment (see Reliability initiatives section).

Reliability initiatives and follow-up actions (after incident):
- Run a focused capacity experiment: shadow additional hot-pool capacity for 48h and measure p99 drift with synthetic traffic.
- Add a telemetry partition to capture per-tenant tail latency; refine tenant-priority heuristics.
- If root cause is cache-warm patterns, create an evaluation to add persistent warm-pool residency for cold models.

Audit and compliance:
- All capacity changes invoked by `terraform` and `ri` must be linked to a PR and use standard approvers.
- For customer-specific Private deployments, record KMS key and access changes in the incident artifacts.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call (short):
- [ ] Confirm p99 breach and burn rate.
- [ ] Run automated triage script and attach snapshots.
- [ ] Apply traffic throttles and circuit breaks.
- [ ] If still degraded, request hot-burst and inform capacity owner.
- [ ] Run synthetic tests and confirm p99 improved.
- [ ] File capacity PR if sustained changes are required.

This doc will be reviewed quarterly and after any incident that required a hot-burst. For questions or improvements, ping the SRE runbook owner (Maya Thompson) or file changes against this page.
